metadata.title: How Much of Every $100 Goes to Health Care?
metadata.section: Section F: Logistics, Infrastructure & Public Health
metadata.data_notes: Uses BEA consumer health spending. The CMS National Health Expenditure data has no API.

series_manifest.label: Consumer Health Care Spending as Share of GDP

events.label: Medicare and Medicaid signed into law
Drugs at their lowest share: 9.3% of health spending
Affordable Care Act signed into law
COVID: delayed care cuts the share to 10.3%

explanation.summary: How much of the whole US economy goes to health care? Measured by what is spent on care for people, it rose from about 3% in 1960 to over 11% today. The share stopped rising around 2010, and prescription drugs are about a sixth of the total.
explanation.methodology: BEA personal consumption expenditures on health care services (DHLCRC1Q027SBEA) divided by GDP, both via FRED, quarterly, filled to monthly. This counts care paid for by households, insurers and Medicare/Medicaid. Prescription drug share = pharmaceutical products spending divided by health services plus pharmaceuticals (BEA annual series). This BEA measure is smaller than the CMS National Health Expenditure total (about 17% of GDP), which also counts investment and public health; that CMS series has no API.

key_findings.title: 1965: Medicare and Medicaid
key_findings.description: When Medicare and Medicaid became law, health care was 3.5% of the economy.
key_findings.significance: Public insurance began four decades of steady growth.

key_findings.title: 2010: Growth Slows
key_findings.description: When the Affordable Care Act became law, the share was 11.3%. It has stayed between about 10.3% and 11.6% since.
key_findings.significance: Health care's share stopped climbing after 2010.

key_findings.title: 2020: The COVID Dip
key_findings.description: The share fell to 10.3% in May 2020 as clinics closed and people delayed care, then recovered to 11.3% by 2024. Drugs reached 18% of health spending in 2020.
key_findings.significance: Even a pandemic did not change the long-run level much.
